Graph: natural-earth-census-2026-grid-v6 · Engine: coarse-road-grid-v6 · Computed in this app

Coverage: Contiguous United States; coarse estimated travel over land and major roads · Completeness unverified

20,474 estimated land cells · 0.05° grid · estimated local travel 25 km/h.

Made with Natural Earth and U.S. Census Bureau 2026 TIGER/Line data. Geo Planner has modified and repackaged Census data into a coarse travel model. This product is not an official Census Bureau product; the Census Bureau has not reviewed or endorsed these estimates.

Natural Earth · U.S. Census Bureau 2026 TIGER/Line

Model note: Very coarse estimate: 0.05° cells (about 3.5–5.5 km) merge nearby roads and crossings. This is display resolution, not a measured accuracy bound.

Model note: Local travel is estimated at 25 km/h, including places without roads. Input access can follow retained road geometry at its assumed class speed after checked local access. Road travel charges retained geometry at assumed 55–105 km/h speeds with approximate transfers inside cells. Nearby roads and crossings merge within cells. No traffic, one-way roads, turn restrictions, terrain or actual access checks.

Model note: Natural Earth and U.S. Census Bureau 2026 TIGER/Line primary/secondary road linework form a modified coarse model, not an official Census product or a routable road inventory. International crossings and ferries are not modeled. Shore connections and road transfers require continuous generalized land. Input access allows up to 1 km of initial shore tolerance; unsupported origins remain isolated. Whole-cell shading can extend across borders or water. Small islands and water crossings can be inaccurate.
